tldr: Your #1 risk detonated: silver crashed to 8-month lows (~$56, -7% wk / -20% mo) and gold slid below $4,000 (~$3,970-4,050, worst week in six) — and, tellingly, they fell DURING a war. The metals are trading as rate/industrial assets, not havens.

The reason is an escalating US-Iran war: a sixth night of US airstrikes and a Hormuz naval blockade drove oil +13% in five days (Brent ~$84, WTI ~$79-82), reviving the inflation/hike fears that pin the Fed — energy is now the leading S&P sector.
June CPI actually landed SOFT (-0.4% m/m, core +2.6%) — the feared hot-core never came — but the oil spike is doing the Fed's hawkish work anyway, which is why metals fell despite the good data.

The AI trade unwound: SOX -11% on the month, SMH -9% in four weeks on capex-peak fears (Burry's chip shorts working). Money rotated OUT of semis INTO energy/financials/industrials — breadth broadened (~69% >200-DMA, best since Feb), so it's a rotation, not a collapse. S&P 7,457 (-1.15%).

Your HK/SGX sleeves held up: HK tech rebounded on AI catalysts (Alibaba +11%, Tencent buyback rolls on, 1.59m shares 6-9 Jul) despite a China Q2 GDP miss (+4.3%); the STI hit a record ~5,553 on a 10-session run.

Regime shifted to 'Hawkish hold meets an oil-shock war', riskOn 0.47→0.45 — disinflation is real but the war's oil spike re-arms the hike tail (~37% July-hike odds); metals and long-duration stay pressured, energy and defensives lead.

regime.label: Hawkish hold meets an oil-shock war
regime.oneLiner: June CPI resolved soft (disinflation), but an escalating US-Iran war spiked oil ~13% and re-armed the Fed's hike tail — so metals and long-duration stay pressured while energy and defensives lead, and an AI-capex unwind rotates money out of semis into cyclicals; the 28-29 July FOMC is the next binary.

topNews.headline: Silver crashes to 8-month lows (~$56, -7% wk / -20% mo) — and it fell DURING the Iran war, not on a safe-haven bid
topNews.actionable: The metal is trading as a rate/industrial asset, not a hedge; keep leverage sized so the break to 8-month lows can't force liquidation, and let the oil-inflation impulse and hike tail fade before any deep-value re-entry.

topNews.headline: Gold slides below $4,000 (~$3,970-4,050), biggest weekly loss in six — but PBoC buys a 20th straight month (+14.93t June)
topNews.actionable: Central-bank demand is a genuine floor near ~$3,900-4,000 for the GDX/miner sleeve, but don't expect gold to rescue silver; both hinge on the oil-inflation impulse and the 28-29 July FOMC.

topNews.headline: US-Iran war spikes oil +13% in five days (Brent ~$84); energy is now the leading S&P sector
topNews.actionable: The war premium lifts energy but is precisely what's crushing the metals book — do NOT add levered silver on the geopolitical spike; watch a ceasefire headline as the fast-reversal risk.

topNews.headline: Semis rout: SOX -11% mo, SMH -9% in 4 wks on AI-capex-peak fears; Burry's chip shorts working, money rotates to cyclicals
topNews.actionable: Don't catch the semis knife (SMH/SMIC); the silver lining is the rotation is INTO energy/financials/industrials, not a broad breakdown — ex-tech breadth stays healthy at ~69% >200-DMA.

topNews.headline: STI hits a record ~5,553 (10th straight up-session); HK tech rebounds on AI despite China Q2 GDP miss (+4.3%)
topNews.actionable: SGX + HK-tech sleeves are the book's bright spot; with SG banks extended at ~2.2x book into results, favor S-REITs (lower SORA), and hold Tencent on its buyback bid. DBS reports ~6 August.
